title: Verify Hot Bin / Hop In behavior using the “indicator” message type (close chute + exchange)
summary: Use this procedure to confirm that totes marked as hop in / hot bin trigger the close chute + exchange behavior, and that the system is using the message type named “indicator” to identify what was marked.
when_to_use: When you need to validate that hop in / hot bin markings cause the expected close chute + exchange behavior, and you need to verify that the marking is associated with the message type called “indicator.”
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Execute the live evidence checks for hop in/hot bin behavior and confirm whether the “indicator” message type is being used for the marking.
access_or_tools_needed: Access to the live system evidence surface that shows the “indicator” message type being sent/processed (exact tool/screen not specified in the packet).

visual_references.description: Training frame showing the hot bin / hop in behavior statements and the “indicator” message type wording.

steps.title: Identify the expected hop in / hot bin behavior and the “indicator” message type
steps.purpose: Establish the exact expected behavior and the message type name that must be evidenced during the live check.
steps.instruction: On the live system evidence surface you will use for troubleshooting, prepare to verify two things: (1) hop in / hot bin markings trigger close chute and exchange, and (2) the marking is associated with the message type explicitly named “indicator.”
steps.expected_result: You can state the expected mapping: hop in/hot bin -> close chute + exchange, and the marking is associated with message type “indicator.”
steps.healthy_condition: The expected behavior mapping is clear and consistent with the provided wording: “Hoppins will trigger all totes that are marked as hop in to close shoots and Exchange” and “It’s literally the message type is called the indicator.”
steps.failure_condition: You cannot align the expected behavior (close chute + exchange) with the message type name “indicator” for the hop in/hot bin marking check.

actions.label: Confirm expected behavior wording
actions.exact_action: Use the provided hot bin/hop in statements and the “indicator” message type wording as the acceptance criteria for the live evidence checks.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “Hoppins will trigger all totes that are marked as hop in to close shoots and Exchange… Hot bins will trigger all totes that are marked as hot bin to close chute and exchange… It’s literally the message type is called the indicator.”

steps.title: Verify the system uses the message type “indicator” for hop in / hot bin marking
steps.purpose: Confirm that the system evidence shows hop in/hot bin marking is tied to the message type named “indicator.”
steps.instruction: Using the live system evidence surface available to you (not specified in the packet), locate evidence that the system received/processed the message type called “indicator” for the hop in/hot bin marking. The packet does not specify the exact UI/log/API location, so use your available evidence surface to find the “indicator” message type label/name.
steps.expected_result: Evidence is found showing the message type “indicator” is used/processed in association with hop in/hot bin marking.
steps.healthy_condition: The evidence explicitly references the message type name “indicator” in the context of hop in/hot bin marking.
steps.failure_condition: No evidence can be found that the message type “indicator” is used/processed for hop in/hot bin marking.

actions.label: Locate “indicator” message type evidence
actions.exact_action: Find and capture the live evidence that the message type is called “indicator” for the hop in/hot bin marking.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if you cannot find evidence of the “indicator” message type being used for the hop in/hot bin marking.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Frame text includes: “Hot bins… once they hit hop in close or hop in disable anything that has an indicator. It’s literally the message type is called the indicator.”

steps.title: Confirm hop in / hot bin totes trigger close chute and exchange
steps.purpose: Validate the core behavior: hop in/hot bin markings must result in close chute and exchange for the marked totes.
steps.instruction: On the live system evidence surface you have available, observe the behavior for totes marked as hop in and totes marked as hot bin. Confirm that those marked totes trigger close chute and exchange behavior.
steps.expected_result: For totes marked as hop in / hot bin, the system triggers close chute and exchange behavior.
steps.healthy_condition: The observed behavior matches the provided mapping: hop in -> close shoots and Exchange; hot bin -> close chute and exchange.
steps.failure_condition: Marked totes do not trigger close chute + exchange as described.

actions.label: Observe close chute + exchange for marked totes
actions.exact_action: Check that totes marked as hop in/hot bin result in close chute and exchange behavior for those totes.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if marked totes do not trigger close chute + exchange as described.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “Hoppins will trigger all totes that are marked as hop in to close shoots and Exchange… Hot bins will trigger all totes that are marked as hot bin to close chute and exchange…”
Frame text includes: “Hot bins will trigger all totes that are marked as hot bin to close chute and exchange.”

steps.title: Check hot bins are treated as highest priority bins
steps.purpose: Confirm the priority intent described for hot bins (highest priority) is reflected in the system behavior you observe.
steps.instruction: Using the live system evidence surface available to you, confirm that hot bin handling is treated as highest priority (i.e., the system is using hot bins to get those totes up to fast). The packet does not specify the exact live signal/field to check, so use the available evidence to determine that hot bin handling is prioritized.
steps.expected_result: Hot bin handling is treated as highest priority in the observed behavior.
steps.healthy_condition: Observed behavior aligns with the provided statement: “Hot bins are the highest priority bins, so they are the ones that I need to get up to fast.”
steps.failure_condition: Hot bin handling does not appear to be treated as highest priority in the observed behavior.

actions.label: Validate priority behavior for hot bins
actions.exact_action: Confirm that hot bin handling is prioritized (highest priority) in the observed system behavior.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “Hot bins are the highest priority bins, so they are the ones that I need to get up to fast.”

steps.title: Escalate if observed behavior does not match documented close chute + exchange and/or “indicator” usage
steps.purpose: Provide the escalation trigger when live evidence does not match the documented behavior mapping.
steps.instruction: If either (a) you cannot find evidence that the message type “indicator” is used for hop in/hot bin marking, or (b) hop in/hot bin marked totes do not trigger close chute + exchange, collect the evidence you can see on your live evidence surface and escalate for deeper troubleshooting.
steps.expected_result: Escalation is initiated with the evidence you collected when mismatches are found.
steps.healthy_condition: Either the behavior matches and no escalation is needed, or mismatches are clearly evidenced and escalated.
steps.failure_condition: Mismatch exists but no escalation is performed despite missing/contradictory evidence.

actions.label: Escalate with collected evidence
actions.exact_action: Escalate for deeper troubleshooting after collecting the evidence you can see regarding “indicator” usage and close chute + exchange behavior.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if you cannot find evidence of the “indicator” message type being used for the hop in/hot bin marking, or if marked totes do not trigger close chute + exchange as described.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Candidate failure/escalation notes: “Escalate if you cannot find evidence of the “indicator” message type being used for the hop in/hot bin marking, or if marked totes do not trigger close chute + exchange as described.”

success_criteria: Evidence shows hop in/hot bin marking is associated with the message type called “indicator.”
Totes marked as hop in/hot bin trigger close chute and exchange behavior.
healthy_conditions: “Hoppins will trigger all totes that are marked as hop in to close shoots and Exchange.”
“Hot bins will trigger all totes that are marked as hot bin to close chute and exchange.”
“It’s literally the message type is called the indicator.”
Hot bins are treated as highest priority bins in observed behavior.
failure_conditions: No evidence of message type “indicator” being used/processed for hop in/hot bin marking.
Totes marked as hop in/hot bin do not trigger close chute + exchange behavior.
Hot bin handling does not appear to be treated as highest priority in observed behavior.
escalation_guidance: Escalate if you cannot find evidence of the “indicator” message type being used for the hop in/hot bin marking, or if marked totes do not trigger close chute + exchange as described.
